newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sydney protest over Bougainville violence.
newsitem.headline: Sydney protest over Bougainville violence.

text.p: Protesters outside the Papua New Guinea consulate in Sydney on Thursday called for the Red Cross and Amnesty International to intervene on Bougainville island after the alleged killing of civilians by PNG defence forces.

Bougainville Freedom Movement secretary Vicki John delivered a letter to consul-general Kila Karo and consul Clement Chikalli calling for international intervention, the withdrawal of PNG forces and self-determination for Bougainville.
"They were actually quite compassionate and said they would contact (PNG) Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan with regard to our demands," John told Reuters.
Thousands of people have died from fighting or disease in the eight year secessionist conflict on Bougainville, 800 km (500 miles) northeast of the PNG capital Port Moresby.

The 25-strong Sydney protest came in the wake of a recent spate of violence on Bougainville, including the death of nine people last month. Media reports said the villagers were killed when mortar shells fell on a bush church.
Papua New Guinea Defence Force Chief-of-Staff Colonel Jack Tuat told Reuters earlier this month he was not aware of the mortar attack at Malapita village on Bougainville.
